No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Welcome to Maracaibo! You'll play as an independent seafarer in the Caribbean seeking wealth and fame through combat, exploration, and strategic card play. Maracaibo is played over 4 rounds. Each round, you and your opponents will sail along a loop around the Caribbean, stopping at cities and villages to take actions. You can stop at as many spaces as you want during a round, but watch out! After any player reaches the end of the loop, the round will end and all players will move back to the start. Contents 1 What To Do On Your Turn 1.1 Phase A - Sailing 1.2 Phase B - Perform Actions 1.3 Phase C - Draw New Cards 2 Main Actions (Phase B) 2.1 Village Spaces 2.1.1 Buying a Card 2.2 City Spaces 2.2.1 Deliveries 2.2.2 Gaining Resources 2.2.3 Exploring 2.2.4 Combat 2.2.5 Combat Notes: 3 Free Actions 3.1 Planning a Card 3.2 Completing a Career Goal 4 Figures 5 End of Round 5.1 Rounds 1 to 3 5.2 Round 4 6 Final Scoring 7 FAQ 7.1 GENERAL 7.2 UPGRADES 7.3 SOLO What To Do On Your Turn On your turn, you will go through these phases in this order: Phase A - Sailing On your turn, you must move 1 to 7 spaces forward in the loop. You may choose to follow either the upper or lower path at a fork. Phase B - Perform Actions You will perform a Main Action at the space you landed on. Each space is either a City or a Village, and this will determine what Main Actions you have available to you. You may also perform any Free Actions. This phase will be the bulk of your turn and is detailed in the next sections. Phase C - Draw New Cards After you’ve performed your actions, you refill your hand to 4 cards (or up to 6 if you have the “Expanded Living Quarters” Ship Upgrade). You may draw cards from the deck for free, or pay 1 Doubloon to draw a card from the face up display. This is also free if you have “Charismatic Leader” Ship Upgrade. After this, it is the next player’s turn. Main Actions (Phase B) Village Spaces When you land on a Village space, you can do one of the following: ● Perform Village Actions based on the number of spaces you moved. ---● 1 to 3 spaces: 1 Village Action ---● 4 to 6 spaces: 2 Village Actions ---● 7 spaces: 3 Village Actions ● Complete a Quest by paying its cost and gaining its effects. Your 4th quest is worth +3 VP and your 5th+ quests are worth +2 VP. ● Use an Assistant’s action You start the game with 3 basic Village Actions: ● Gain 1 Doubloon ● Discard your entire hand for 2 Doubloons ● Buy a card Buying a Card When buying a card, you pay its cost (Doubloons, goods, and/or combat points) and then gain any bonuses: ● Green Scrolls: Doubloon or VP Production. You will increase your production by the amount shown. You start the game with 0 VP Production and 8 Doubloon Production. You will gain this at the start of each round. Some production bonuses are locked until you gain the required synergy token. If you would gain Doubloon production beyond 34, all subsequent Doubloon production is converted to VP Production. ● Tan Scrolls: Immediate bonuses. Gain a number of Figures, Combat Points, etc. ● Synergy Tokens: You gain the depicted synergy token. These unlock production on cards that show a matching synergy token requirement. You can only gain 1 of each synergy token, but you may still play multiple cards that provide a given synergy token. Gaining a synergy token activates any production bonuses you have that needed this token. ● Red Scrolls: Passive Effects. These are ongoing effects or abilities that you can use at the specified time: ---● Last Village Actions can be used as the final village action whenever you receive a village actions ---● New combat actions to use once per Combat phase ---● Bonuses that give you additional exploration steps when you explore, or an extra combat point w

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] The game is awash in symbols that require constant head scratching and referral to the rulebook. This makes it difficult to learn and ultimately only works if you play it frequently enough to remember what the icons mean. At least the cards have some text. Clearly not well thought out from the user interface perspective.

[Rating: 1/10] There's only 2 non-white characters in this game among multitudes of characters that are very white. Is it racist? I don't know but I really don't like that.

[Rating: 1/10] Another of the medium heads down Euros that didn't register. Wouldn't return to it. + Different valid point strategies available - cards, combat and exploring. + Hint of a story in the campaign game. - Theme is pasted on - Board is cluttered - Random card draw is extremely annoying - Doesn't have the exciting arc that you feel in Great Western Trail  - Tiny stacked discs on player boards are too small - Game felt long even with rushing end game >2.5 hours without including setup or pack away

[Rating: 1/10] :star::nostar::nostar::nostar::nostar:  Another boring modern Euro with little player interaction and so many mini games taped together, where efficiency is the name of the game.   Good or even great for some, but this is just absolutely dull to me nowadays when I can just play any Splotter title.

[Rating: 1/10] Another game of genre: „let’s put maximum abstract elements to the rulebook and let’s pretend they all work together”. But all of this is simply a fake to keep euro geeks excited. After dozens of similar heavy non-sense euros I worked out my own strategy to play such games and not get crazy. I don’t calculate anything because in such overabundance of abstract factors it’s not possible to play consciously. How can you evaluate in the middle of the game whether the advance on one track is more profitable than erecting the building? You can’t. Especially when almost each element of the game may g

[Rating: 1/10] Enjoyable but mostly dull and unremarkable rondel point salad tableau building race, for all of the rules and fiddly setup the game itself is fairly simple and as a result the decisions are too obvious and straight forward to be an interesting optimization puzzle. Unfortunately the one exciting thing about the game, the multi use cardplay, is hampered by the too strong luck of the draw as the game goes by too quickly with competent players for there to be enough turns for the randomness to even out.

[Rating: 1/10] Lake Maracaibo has the most lightning strikes on the planet! That's not in the game, I learned it elsewhere. Here you're just collecting coins and VPs while ignoring everything interesting.  On the bright side, you can rush the ending if you want this over faster. Most games don't allow you that mercy!

[Rating: 2/10] Forget the designer and its previous designs there are both good.  About Maracaibo: This game was not fully developed, seems rushed, good concepts that just don't shine, gameplay is boring, actions are dull, also: the iconography is terrible,  the setup tedious the interaction is zero downtime is huge numbers feel random (1-7 movement, 1-3x action...) 1 billion cards that do boring same things over and over combat action is unnecessarily complicated   ...  Don't get the hype.

[Rating: 2/10] It's just another very and unecessarily heavy game.  With extraordinary setup time and a hefty instruction tome it just doesn't fit my gaming interests.  It looks like it might have potential with the legacy component but not a huge fan of that either.  So off to the 'for sale' pile it goes. Maracaibo?  Maracai-no!

[Rating: 2/10] The colonizing theme without consequence and lack of diversity within the game cards really just ruined the experience for me. The rules tried to state they abstracted the horribleness out of the game which seemed even more like whitewashing the whole situation while continuing to exploit the region and events of history for personal gain.  I guess I want a game that is more considerate and less callous about these things.
